Read and strictly follow /AGENTS.md (Vietnamese) before suggesting or generating any code.

Summary:
- Source of truth: Google Sheet "BacklogSOA" (mirror: docs/backlog/*.csv). Sheet `01_AI_RULES` wins over any suggestion.
- Architecture: SOA microservices with Spring Boot + Spring MVC layers (controller -> service -> repository) exactly as listed in `09_Service_Catalog`. No hexagonal/clean architecture, CQRS, event sourcing, WebFlux or GraphQL. No cross-schema DB access.
- Names, APIs, tables and columns need no approval: first search `11_Naming_Registry` / `10_API_Contract` / `12_Data_Dictionary` and reuse an existing name with the same meaning; if none exists, add a new row (status Approved) in the same PR and use it. CI only requires that a name is registered; old names and Deprecated names are blocked. When renaming, update the registry (old name column, Renamed) and `15_Change_Log` in the same PR, plus the API contract if another package uses it.
- Code screens against the approved wireframes (all 64 are "Đã duyệt"). Do not invent business rules: the package owner decides package-local questions; cross-package questions go to an open question with a proposed answer (accepted after 24h without objection).
- Each member codes every story of their package in one go. If another package is not built yet, declare a placeholder from the contract (R-37): a client interface + DTO (or event payload) with the exact names/paths from `09`/`10`/`11` inside your own service, mocked with Mockito/WireMock in tests, a `StubXxxClient` only under `@Profile("stub")`, and MSW on the web. When the other package ships, switch the stub off; no code merge is needed. Green CI means the author merges; only cross-package contract changes, edits to shared code (`homecare-common`, `src/shared/ui`, `src/app`) and core security need the owner notified (R-35, R-36).
- Frontend: one React web app in `frontend/` (Vite + React 19 + TypeScript strict, TanStack Query, Zustand, React Hook Form + Zod, React Router, Tailwind + Radix, own `Hc*` components in `src/shared/ui`). No mobile app, no Redux, no Next.js/SSR, no other UI kit, no CSS-in-JS. Never store tokens in the browser: the api-gateway is the BFF (HttpOnly session cookie + CSRF). Pages must be responsive (works at 390px).
